LESSON: PLC motor start stop seal-in
1. The seal-in (or "latching") rung is the core of a motor starter. It uses the output contact of the motor coil (or a relay controlling it) to feed back into the start circuit. This allows the motor to run even after the Start button is released.
2. The circuit must include a Normally Open (NO) Start button, a Normally Closed (NC) Stop button, and an Overload contact (which is also NC).
3. In Ladder Logic (rung text), the logic is: (Start OR Seal-In) AND NOT Stop AND NOT Overload.
4. The "Seal-In" contact is the output of the coil itself. The Stop and Overload contacts break the circuit if pressed or tripped.
5. The output coil energizes when the logic is true, which then closes the Seal-In contact to maintain the state.

QUOTE [1]: The seal-in (or "latching") rung is the core of a motor starter. It uses the output contact of the motor coil (or a relay controlling it) to feed back into the start circuit. This allows the motor to run even after the Start button is released.
QUOTE [2]: The circuit must include a Normally Open (NO) Start button, a Normally Closed (NC) Stop button, and an Overload contact (which is also NC).
QUOTE [3]: In Ladder Logic (rung text), the logic is: (Start OR Seal-In) AND NOT Stop AND NOT Overload.
QUOTE [4]: The "Seal-In" contact is the output of the coil itself. The Stop and Overload contacts break the circuit if pressed or tripped.
QUOTE [5]: The output coil energizes when the logic is true, which then closes the Seal-In contact to maintain the state.

Here is the rung text for the motor start/stop with seal-in:

MAKE CODE: Motor Start/Stop Ladder Logic
language ladder
    [XIC(Start) ,XIC(SealIn) ]XIO(Stop)XIO(Overload)OTE(Motor);
END
Lantern checks it (brackets, a missing ;, colons and indents, pins never set as outputs, undeclared PLC variables ...) and sends back what it finds once. Explain in comments inside the code, briefly; never think
aloud in comments. Ladder is rung text, one rung per line ending with ; and [A ,B ] is a branch (OR):
    [XIC(Start) ,XIC(Motor) ]XIC(Stop)OTE(Motor);
XIC is true while the input is on, XIO while it is off. A normally closed Stop button (or overload contact) keeps
its input on until it is pressed (or trips), so it is examined with XIC; XIO there would never let the motor run.

The code provided is correct for the requested logic.
- `[XIC(Start) ,XIC(SealIn) ]`: This creates the OR condition. The motor starts if the Start button is pressed OR if the Seal-In contact is closed (which happens when the motor is already running).
- `XIO(Stop)`: This checks the Stop button. Since it is Normally Closed, it is "on" (true) when not pressed. `XIO` means "Input is Off", so if the Stop button is pressed (open), the rung breaks.
- `XIO(Overload)`: Same as Stop. If the overload trips (opens), the rung breaks.
- `OTE(Motor)`: This energizes the Motor coil if the entire rung is true.

ANSWER: The ladder logic rung text is [XIC(Start) ,XIC(SealIn) ]XIO(Stop)XIO(Overload)OTE(Motor);
